## 📜 Full A–Z list


### A

**A/B test** · 📊 Statistics  
A controlled experiment that randomly splits users between two versions and compares an outcome. Example: Half of visitors see a new checkout button; compare conversion rates.

**Accuracy** · 📏 Evaluation  
The share of predictions that are correct. Misleading when one class is rare. Example: 99% accuracy on fraud data can mean the model never flags fraud.

**Activation function** · 🧠 Deep learning  
A non-linear function applied to a neuron's output so networks can learn curves, not just lines. Example: ReLU returns max(0, x).

**Anomaly detection** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Finding data points that look very different from the rest. Example: Flagging a server whose CPU pattern suddenly changes.

**API** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
A defined way for programs to talk to each other, often over HTTP. Example: POST a payment as JSON, get back a fraud score.

**AUC (ROC AUC)** · 📏 Evaluation  
The probability that the model ranks a random positive above a random negative. 0.5 is random, 1.0 is perfect. Example: A churn model with AUC 0.82.


### B

**Backpropagation** · 🧠 Deep learning  
The algorithm that computes how much each weight contributed to the error, so gradient descent can update it. Example: Errors flow backward from the output layer to the first layer.

**Bagging** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Training many models on random resamples of the data and averaging them to reduce variance. Example: A random forest is bagged decision trees plus random feature choice.

**Batch inference** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Scoring many records at once on a schedule instead of one request at a time. Example: Nightly churn scores for every customer.

**Bayes' theorem** · 📊 Statistics  
A rule for updating the probability of a belief after seeing evidence. Example: Updating the chance of disease after a positive test.

**Bias (statistical)** · 📊 Statistics  
A systematic difference between an estimate and the true value. Example: Surveying only app users overestimates tech comfort.

**Bias-variance trade-off** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Simple models miss patterns (bias); complex models chase noise (variance). Good models balance both. Example: A straight line underfits; a degree-20 polynomial overfits.

**Bootstrap** · 📊 Statistics  
Estimating uncertainty by resampling the data with replacement many times. Example: 1,000 resamples give a confidence interval for the median.

**Bounding box** · 👁️ Computer vision  
A rectangle that marks where an object is in an image. Example: x, y, width, height around each car.


### C

**Canary release** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Sending a small share of traffic to a new version before rolling it out fully. Example: 5% of payments go to model v15 first.

**Categorical variable** · 🧹 Data  
A variable whose values are labels, not numbers. Example: Plan type: basic, plus, premium.

**Central limit theorem** · 📊 Statistics  
Averages of many independent samples are approximately normal, whatever the original distribution. Example: Daily average order values look bell-shaped.

**Classification** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Predicting a category. Example: Spam or not spam.

**Clustering** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Grouping similar items without labels. Example: k-means groups customers by behaviour.

**CNN** · 🧠 Deep learning  
A convolutional neural network: layers of small filters that detect patterns in images. Example: Early layers find edges, later layers find faces.

**Concept drift** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
When the relationship between inputs and the target changes over time. Example: Fraudsters switch to small test payments.

**Confidence interval** · 📊 Statistics  
A range that would contain the true value in a stated share (e.g. 95%) of repeated studies. Example: Conversion 4.1% ± 0.3%.

**Confusion matrix** · 📏 Evaluation  
A table of true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives. Example: Shows which mistakes a classifier makes.

**Container** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
A packaged app with its libraries that runs the same everywhere. Example: A Docker image of a FastAPI model service.

**Correlation** · 📊 Statistics  
A number from -1 to 1 measuring how strongly two variables move together in a straight line. Example: Height and weight: r ≈ 0.7. Correlation is not causation.

**Cross-validation** · 📏 Evaluation  
Splitting data into k folds and training k times, each time testing on a different fold. Example: 5-fold CV gives five scores; report their mean.


### D

**Data drift** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
When the distribution of input data changes compared with training data. Example: Average payment size doubles after a new market launch.

**Data leakage** · 🧹 Data  
When information unavailable at prediction time sneaks into training, inflating scores. Example: Using 'account closed date' to predict churn.

**Data pipeline** · 🧹 Data  
An automated chain of steps that moves and transforms data. Example: Extract from API, clean, load to a warehouse.

**Decision tree** · 🤖 Machine learning  
A model that makes predictions by asking a sequence of yes/no questions. Example: Is tenure < 6 months? Is plan month-to-month?

**Deep learning** · 🧠 Deep learning  
Machine learning with neural networks that have many layers. Example: Image recognition, speech, language models.

**Dimensionality reduction** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Compressing many features into fewer while keeping most information. Example: PCA turns 50 survey questions into 3 factors.

**Dropout** · 🧠 Deep learning  
Randomly switching off neurons during training to reduce overfitting. Example: Dropout rate 0.3 in a dense layer.


### E

**Embedding** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
A list of numbers that represents a word, sentence, image or item so that similar things are close together. Example: 'king' and 'queen' have nearby embeddings.

**Ensemble** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Combining several models to get better predictions than any single one. Example: Averaging a forest, a boosted model and a linear model.

**Epoch** · 🧠 Deep learning  
One full pass of the training data through the model. Example: Train for 20 epochs.

**ETL / ELT** · 🧹 Data  
Extract, transform, load: moving data from sources into a store. ELT loads first and transforms inside the warehouse. Example: Daily sales from the shop database to BigQuery.


### F

**F1 score** · 📏 Evaluation  
The harmonic mean of precision and recall. Example: Useful when both false alarms and misses matter.

**Feature** · 🧹 Data  
An input variable used by a model. Example: Tenure, monthly charge, number of support calls.

**Feature engineering** · 🧹 Data  
Creating new, more useful inputs from raw data. Example: Turning timestamps into 'hour of day' and 'is weekend'.

**Feature store** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
A system that stores and serves features consistently for training and prediction. Example: The same 'tx_last_hour' value used offline and online.

**Fine-tuning** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset. Example: Adapting a general language model to support tickets.


### G

**Gradient boosting** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Building trees one after another, each fixing the errors of the previous ones. Example: XGBoost, LightGBM, scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting.

**Gradient descent** · 🤖 Machine learning  
An optimisation method that repeatedly steps weights in the direction that reduces the loss. Example: Learning rate 0.01, 1,000 steps.


### H

**Hallucination** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
When a generative model states something fluent but false. Example: Inventing a citation that does not exist.

**Hyperparameter** · 🤖 Machine learning  
A setting chosen before training, not learned from data. Example: Tree depth, learning rate, number of clusters.

**Hypothesis test** · 📊 Statistics  
A procedure for judging whether data are consistent with a default assumption (the null hypothesis). Example: Is the new page's conversion rate really higher?


### I

**Imbalanced data** · 🧹 Data  
When one class is much rarer than the others. Example: 0.2% of transactions are fraud.

**Imputation** · 🧹 Data  
Filling in missing values. Example: Replace missing income with the median.

**Inference** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Using a trained model to make predictions. (In statistics, it means drawing conclusions from data.) Example: The API runs inference in 20 ms.

**IoU** · 👁️ Computer vision  
Intersection over union: how much a predicted box overlaps the true box, from 0 to 1. Example: IoU ≥ 0.5 often counts as a correct detection.


### K

**k-nearest neighbours** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Predicting by looking at the k most similar training examples. Example: A house is priced like its 5 nearest neighbours.


### L

**Label** · 🧹 Data  
The correct answer the model learns to predict. Example: 'churned' = 1 or 0.

**Large language model (LLM)** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
A very large neural network trained on text to predict the next token, able to generate and reason over language. Example: Chat assistants and coding assistants.

**Latency** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
How long one request takes. Example: p95 latency of 60 ms.

**Learning rate** · 🧠 Deep learning  
How big a step gradient descent takes each update. Example: Too high diverges, too low crawls.

**Linear regression** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Predicting a number as a weighted sum of inputs. Example: Price = 50,000 + 120 × square feet.

**Logistic regression** · 🤖 Machine learning  
A linear model passed through a sigmoid to predict a probability. Example: Probability that a customer churns.

**Loss function** · 🤖 Machine learning  
A number that measures how wrong the model is; training tries to make it small. Example: Mean squared error, cross-entropy.


### M

**MAE** · 📏 Evaluation  
Mean absolute error: average size of errors in the target's units. Example: Forecasts are off by 12 units on average.

**mAP** · 👁️ Computer vision  
Mean average precision: the standard accuracy score for object detectors. Example: COCO mAP 50:95 of 54.7.

**MLOps** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Practices that automate and monitor training, testing, deployment and retraining of ML models. Example: A pipeline retrains monthly and gates releases.

**Model registry** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
A catalogue of model versions with metrics, lineage and aliases. Example: 'payguard@champion' points to version 15.

**Monitoring** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Watching a live system's health, data and quality over time. Example: Alert when PSI > 0.2.

**Multicollinearity** · 📊 Statistics  
When input variables are strongly correlated with each other, making coefficients unstable. Example: House size in square feet and in square metres.


### N

**Naive Bayes** · 🤖 Machine learning  
A fast probabilistic classifier that assumes features are independent given the class. Example: A classic spam filter.

**Neural network** · 🧠 Deep learning  
Layers of simple units connected by weights that together learn complex functions. Example: Input layer → hidden layers → output.

**Normal distribution** · 📊 Statistics  
The symmetric bell curve described by a mean and standard deviation. Example: About 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations.

**Normalisation / scaling** · 🧹 Data  
Rescaling features to a common range or spread. Example: StandardScaler gives mean 0, standard deviation 1.

**Null hypothesis** · 📊 Statistics  
The default assumption a test tries to find evidence against. Example: 'The new design has no effect.'


### O

**One-hot encoding** · 🧹 Data  
Turning a category into several 0/1 columns. Example: Plan → is_basic, is_plus, is_premium.

**Outlier** · 🧹 Data  
A value far from most others. Example: A $50,000 order in a shop where most are $40.

**Overfitting** · 🤖 Machine learning  
When a model memorises training data and performs poorly on new data. Example: Training accuracy 99%, test accuracy 70%.


### P

**p-value** · 📊 Statistics  
The probability of seeing results at least this extreme if the null hypothesis were true. Example: p = 0.03 is unusual under 'no effect'. It is not the chance the null is true.

**PCA** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Principal component analysis: finds new axes that capture the most variance. Example: Plot 100 features in 2D.

**Precision** · 📏 Evaluation  
Of the items flagged positive, the share that really are positive. Example: Of 100 flagged payments, 80 were fraud: precision 0.8.

**Prompt** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
The input text or instructions given to a generative model. Example: 'Summarise this ticket in one sentence.'

**PSI** · 🚀 Deployment & MLOps  
Population stability index: a score of how much a feature's distribution has shifted. Example: Above 0.2 usually needs attention.


### R

**RAG** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant documents, then let an LLM answer using them. Example: A help bot that cites your own docs.

**Random forest** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Many decision trees trained on random samples and features, averaged together. Example: A strong default for tabular data.

**Recall** · 📏 Evaluation  
Of all real positives, the share the model found. Example: Caught 90 of 100 frauds: recall 0.9.

**Regression** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Predicting a number. Example: Next week's sales.

**Regularisation** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Adding a penalty for complexity to reduce overfitting. Example: L2 (ridge) shrinks coefficients; L1 (lasso) can zero them.

**Reinforcement learning** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Learning by trial and error to maximise a reward. Example: A robot learns to walk; a model learns from human feedback.

**RMSE** · 📏 Evaluation  
Root mean squared error: like MAE but punishes large errors more. Example: RMSE of 15 units.


### S

**Sampling** · 📊 Statistics  
Selecting a subset of a population to study. Example: Survey 1,000 of 1 million customers at random.

**Segmentation (image)** · 👁️ Computer vision  
Labelling every pixel with a class or object. Example: Masks for road, car, pedestrian.

**Sigmoid** · 🧠 Deep learning  
An S-shaped function that squeezes any number into 0–1. Example: Turns a score into a probability.

**Standard deviation** · 📊 Statistics  
The typical distance of values from the mean. Example: Delivery times: mean 3 days, SD 1 day.

**Stratified split** · 📏 Evaluation  
A train/test split that keeps class proportions the same in each part. Example: Both splits keep 15% churners.

**Supervised learning** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Learning from examples that have correct answers (labels). Example: Past emails labelled spam / not spam.


### T

**Test set** · 📏 Evaluation  
Data held back until the end to estimate real-world performance. Example: Never tune on it.

**Time series** · 🧹 Data  
Data points recorded in time order. Example: Daily website visits.

**Token** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
A chunk of text (word or word piece) that a language model reads and writes. Example: 'unbelievable' → 'un', 'believ', 'able'.

**Train/validation/test split** · 📏 Evaluation  
Separate data for learning, tuning and final evaluation. Example: 70% / 15% / 15%.

**Transfer learning** · 🧠 Deep learning  
Reusing a model trained on one task as the starting point for another. Example: ImageNet CNN fine-tuned to spot defects.

**Transformer** · 💬 NLP & GenAI  
A neural architecture built on attention, the basis of modern language and vision models. Example: BERT, GPT, ViT, DETR.

**Type I / Type II error** · 📊 Statistics  
Type I: a false alarm (rejecting a true null). Type II: a miss (failing to reject a false null). Example: Approving a useless drug vs missing a useful one.


### U

**Underfitting** · 🤖 Machine learning  
When a model is too simple to capture the pattern. Example: A straight line through a curved relationship.

**Unsupervised learning** · 🤖 Machine learning  
Finding structure in data without labels. Example: Clustering, dimensionality reduction.


### V

**Validation set** · 📏 Evaluation  
Data used to choose hyperparameters and compare models. Example: Pick the tree depth with the best validation AUC.


### W

**Weight** · 🧠 Deep learning  
A learned number that scales an input's influence on a neuron or model output. Example: In y = 3x + 2, the weight is 3.


### Y

**YOLO** · 👁️ Computer vision  
'You Only Look Once': a family of fast single-pass object detectors. Example: Real-time detection on a phone or camera.
